name: Westcliff University (WU)
overview:
Founded in 1993, and based in Irvine, California, Westcliff University is globally recognized and accredited.

Westcliff offers undergraduate and graduate certificates and degree programs in the areas of Business, Education, Technology & Engineering, and Law. WU prepares students for personal, professional, and academic success through innovative, up-to-date, and high-quality programs. International students have the opportunity to start 6x per year and study together with American and other international students from across the globe and form networks for a lifetime.

The Greater Los Angeles area is the second-largest metropolitan area in the U.S. and is a home to several world-famous landmarks and attractions, including the Hollywood Walk of Fame, Disneyland, and Universal Studios. Located close to several beautiful California beaches, Irvine is about an hour away from L.A. and has consistently been ranked as one of the safest cities in the U.S. based on FBI crime statistics. Irvine and its surrounding areas offer a diverse range of activities such as hiking, surfing, shopping, dining, and entertainment options such as Irvine Spectrum Center, the Orange County Fair, and more.
administrative:
1. Application dossier

You will work directly with the partner university regarding your application. All required documents must be uploaded on their platform or sent by email before the deadline. (See the Americas Teams channel for each application deadline.). If you have not received anything yet, it means your nomination has not been sent yet — please be patient.


The partner may ask for the following:

  • Official Transcripts in English (stamped & signed by home institution)
  • Passport copy (valid 6 months after the program end date)
  • Proof of Financial Support in English
  • Health Insurance is mandatory

This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.

To be given to Epitech bachelor campus administration to reenroll for the Tech4 (in April/May):

  • The addendum to the contract.
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier.


2. Visa

You can find all the detailed information on the US government website or the Embassy of the US in Paris website. You can check the deadlines for obtaining an appointment here.


1/Admission letter and I-20 form

Once you are admitted by the host university, WU will send us your admission package with your acceptance letter & original documents for your visa. You can request a visa only after your application has been approved. Please check the information on I-20 carefully and sign the document.


2/Pay the SEVIS fees

You must then pay the SEVIS I-901 fees online (here). Make sure you print the receipts. The fees for students are $350.


3/Complete the DS-160 form

Complete DS-160 form and upload an ID photo meeting the following requirements. Print the application form confirmation page to bring to your interview.

You will have to pay a visa application fee (non refundable) before your interview of $185 (more information here).


4/Schedule an appointment at the consulate

For people in France, you need to make an appointment for your interview at the US Consulate. Plan to travel to Paris for it.

If you live in another country, check the different consulate/embassy.


During your interview at the consulate, you must:

  • have the necessary supporting documents to prove that you qualify for the category of visa that you request--document relating to your current studies and its relationship to the studies you wish to pursue in the United States: academic transcript, various certificates, SAT or TOEFL test scores, diplomas, etc.
  • demonstrate, with supporting evidence, to the consular officer that you have solid family, social and financial ties to France and that you intend to return there once your residence permit has expired.
  • prove that you have the financial means necessary to finance your studies and live in good conditions in the United States for the first 12 months. Any document proving your family or relational ties with any person funding your studies, as well as bank statements, tax notices thereof.

Please note that the visa gives you the right to work 20 hours on campus.


3.Insurance and Health (more information here, at the bottom of the page)

International students have the option of choosing health insurance plans that are recommended by Westcliff University, or they can choose a health insurance provider from their home country. The International Student Office is happy to assist you in finding a perfect fit for your health insurance provider.


It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.


For more information, you can consult the country’s health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/etats-unis

Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.


4. Prepare your arrival

A welcoming and eventful orientation day is organized for all international students about one week prior to the beginning of courses to make the start as smooth as possible and to familiarize students with their fellow classmates, the campus and professors, as well as their class schedule.

For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on the host country, click here. 

Check out this page which has information for international students given by the university.

Important Notes:

  • Credit Check: Many landlords will check your credit history to determine your financial reliability. This often requires you to provide your SSN. If you have limited or no credit history, landlords may ask for a co-signer to guarantee the lease. The co-signer will be responsible for rent if you are unable to pay.
  • International Students: If you do not have a U.S. credit history or SSN, some landlords may require alternative documentation, such as proof of income or a
  • larger security deposit.
  • Security Deposit: Be prepared to pay a security deposit, typically equivalent to one or two months’ rent. This is held by the landlord to cover any damages or unpaid rent.
  • Utilities: Some rental agreements may include utilities (water, electricity, gas, etc.), but many will require you to set up and pay for utilities on your own. Confirm this with the landlord before signing the lease agreement.
courses:
Credits

Students must take 30 credits over the academic year in order to obtain 60 ECTS.


Academic calendar

Students must arrive for the first session which starts at the beginning of September.


Department and Courses

You will be enrolled in the BSIT program. After your year at Westcliff you will earn a degree in BSIT with a concentration in Advanced Programming.


Courses to be taken at Westcliff to earn the degree:

  • DATA 210 - Database Design & Analytics
  • NET 300 - Cloud Computing
  • NET 200 - Network Routing & Switching
  • TECH 300 - Internet of Things
  • TECH 310 - Management of Information Systems
  • DATA 400 - Data Driven Systems Design and Optimization
  • TECH 400 - Applied System Integration
  • LDR 300 - Introduction to Leadership
  • LDR 303 - Foundations in Operations Management
  • CAP 490 - Capstone Project


Final grades are determined by attendance and class participation, discussion questions, professional assignments, course learning assessments, team projects, etc.


You may eventually request to take courses not on this list by creating a Zammad ticket with your request.


Important notes

  • Presence in class is compulsory, under penalty of loss of visa and repatriation to France at the student's expense (impact on credits).
  • The courses are most likely more academic than at EPITECH.
  • The course list is given for information only. It can change from year to year.
  • If a course is not available when you arrive on site, EPITECH cannot be held responsible for it.
  • Any Tech 4 abroad involves an EIP! Take advantage of the free slots you will have to advance it.
cost:
Financial Overview (4th year Epitech)

  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • EPITECH covers the tuition fees. Epitech covers tuition only for required credits.
  • The tuition supplement payable by you is indicated at the top of this page (if applicable).
  • Other costs at your expense include: travel, accommodation on site, insurance, and everyday expenses (books, food, transport, etc.).


Other Expenses / Estimated Budget (more information here)

The local currency is the Dollar. 1 € = 1.16USD (rate as of October 2025).


Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.


The estimated costs from Westcliff University are about 1,700 USD per month (including rent, living expenses and transportation).

  • Round trip flights: about 1000€, depending on the airline & travel dates
  • Health insurance: $2500/year (university insurance) / 300-600€ for an additional international insurance depending on the company & coverage
  • Visa application fees: about 500€
  • Books, course materials, supplies, equipment: $1000
  • Housing: 13 500$/year
  • Food: 6500$/year
  • Transportation: 1700$/year
  • Leisure: 4500$/year


These prices are indicative and may vary.



Academic training / paid internship

Please note that starting from Semester 2, J1 students are eligible to apply for Academic Training (AT), or paid internship. This work permit is valid for the same length as the study period. The WU Career Center will be happy to help you find a suitable company for such an internship.


Scholarship

International students studying abroad at WU can also apply for a study abroad scholarship.
